# Agent API coverage

<!-- Generated by scripts/agent-api-coverage.js from electron/mcp/agent/registry.js.
     Do not edit by hand: `npm run agent:coverage` rewrites it, and the Agent API
     test fails when it is out of date. -->

Every project-semantic thing Stacki can do, and what an agent can do with it.
The first table is the surface; the second is what is deliberately not on it,
and why. A capability in neither table is an oversight, and `test/agent-api.js`
says so.

“Needs” is the lowest agent-access level that may run the operation — see
[agent-api.md](agent-api.md) for what the levels mean.

## target

| Action | Needs | Where | Undo | Reuses | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | Inspect | renderer | — | src/agent/targetRead.js over the live editor model | Everything Stacki knows about one editor object: source trail, props, classes, bindings, styles, occurrence. |
| `select` | Inspect | renderer | — | App.jsx selection + occurrence request | Select a target in Stacki, so get_context and capture describe it. |
| `enter` | Inspect | renderer | — | App.jsx openComponent | Open a component instance and read inside its own file — what a double-click does. |
| `exit` | Inspect | renderer | — | App.jsx closeComponent | Come back out of a component to whatever contains it. |
| `edit` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js through App.jsx mutateModel | Several operations on one target as a single undo step, all validated before any is applied. |
| `set_text` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js setText | Replace a node's own text. |
| `set_prop` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js setProp | Set one prop or attribute. |
| `remove_prop` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js setProp | Remove a prop or attribute. |
| `set_classes` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/classAttr.js | Replace the element's class list. |
| `add_class` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/classAttr.js withClass | Add one class. |
| `remove_class` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/classAttr.js | Remove one class. |
| `insert_before` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js insertIntoModel | Insert a new node before the target. |
| `insert_after` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js insertIntoModel | Insert a new node after the target. |
| `append_child` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js insertIntoModel | Insert a new node as the target's last child. |
| `remove` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js removeNode | Delete the target, its note, and frontmatter nothing else reads. |
| `duplicate` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js duplicateNode | Copy the target in beside itself. |
| `move` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js moveNode | Move the target somewhere else in the tree. |
| `set_tag` | Edit project | renderer | ⌘Z | src/modelOps.js setTag | Change an element's tag, keeping the attributes the new tag understands. |

## Deliberately not exposed

| Capability | Why | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project:openDialog`<br>`project:newDialog`<br>`project:parentDialog` | human-only | Native folder and file pickers. An agent cannot see one, and which project is open is the person’s decision to make. |
| `assets:pickUpload` | human-only | A native picker over the whole filesystem — the one door in Stacki that reaches outside the open project, and it opens only for a person. |
| `assets:upload` | human-only | Copies files in from anywhere on the machine. Its input is a picker result or a drag, neither of which an agent has. |
| `shell:openExternal` | human-only | Opens a browser on this machine. An agent that wants a page read has its own way to fetch one. |
| `native:copy`<br>`native:paste`<br>`native:undo`<br>`native:redo` | human-only | The operating system’s edit menu acting on whichever text field has focus. project.undo is the editor’s own stack, which is the one that means something here. |
| `clipboard:write` | human-only | Puts text on the machine’s clipboard, for the one thing that needs it: a person pressing Copy on a secure share invitation. An agent that could write the clipboard could put an invitation somewhere nobody chose to put it. |
| `settings:get` | redundant | Application preferences — the sound setting, and this API’s own permission mode, which get_capabilities already reports. |
| `settings:setAgentMode`<br>`settings:agentAccess` | human-only | How much of Stacki an agent may move, and what it currently is. An agent that could raise its own permission level would not have one; get_capabilities tells it what it has. |
| `terminal:start`<br>`terminal:resize`<br>`terminal:close` | unsafe | An agent connected to Stacki already has its own shell. A second one behind this endpoint would widen what a stolen token is worth and buy nothing visual. |
| `project:scaffold`<br>`project:createAstro`<br>`project:createStarter` | human-only | Creating a project decides where it lives on disk and runs the Astro installer. This API acts on the project that is already open. |
| `project:close` | human-only | Closes the project and reloads the window — it would pull the ground out from under the agent’s own refs mid-call. |
| `project:pending` | redundant | The internal handshake for a window that is reloading onto another project. |
| `watch:start` | redundant | The file watcher starts when a project opens; there is nothing here for anybody to decide. |
| `recents:list`<br>`recents:add`<br>`recents:remove`<br>`recents:refreshThumb` | human-only | The welcome screen’s own list of projects and their pictures. Not project state, and not about the project that is open. |
| `preview:atCommit`<br>`preview:stop` | human-only | Points the canvas at a throwaway checkout and makes the editor read-only. An agent driving it would be an agent editing files that are about to be deleted. |
| `reviews:sharedEnable`<br>`reviews:sharedJoin`<br>`reviews:sharedDisable`<br>`reviews:sharedInvite` | unsafe | Creating a workspace, joining one or minting an invitation decides who can read somebody’s private comments. A person types the server address and the invitation. |
| `reviews:identity`<br>`reviews:setIdentity` | unsafe | Changing whose name is on a comment. An agent signs with its own, and cannot sign with anybody else’s. |
| `reviews:editMessage`<br>`reviews:removeMessage` | human-only | Rewording and pruning are a person tidying their own notes. An agent that could rewrite the conversation is an agent whose record of it means nothing. |
| `reviews:remove` | unsafe | Deleting somebody’s feedback. An agent that disagrees resolves the thread with its reasoning, which leaves them able to disagree back. |
| `reviews:recolor` | human-only | The colour the user files a comment under. Their filing, not a state to act on. |
| `reviews:sync`<br>`reviews:syncAnchors`<br>`reviews:shared` | redundant | Housekeeping the window does for itself; get_comments already reports the result of all of it. |
| `reviews:list`<br>`reviews:act` | exposed elsewhere | These ARE get_comments and comment, which existed before this feature and are unchanged by it. |
| `selection:copy` | redundant | Puts the selection trail on the clipboard for pasting into a chat. get_context and target.read return the same trail as data. |
| `page:write`<br>`page:writeRaw`<br>`page:parseSource` | exposed elsewhere | The model and raw writers, and the parse that turns text into a model without touching disk. Reached through target edits and source writes, which go through the editor so undo, the canvas and the preview all follow. |
| `style:listFiles`<br>`style:listAstroStyles` | exposed elsewhere | The stylesheet scan the Style panel runs. style.read and style.list_sources answer from it, with the rules already matched against the element. |
| `mcp:publish`<br>`mcp:reply`<br>`mcp:status` | redundant | The wiring between this server and its own window. Nothing about the project is in any of it. |

## Totals

- 8 domains, 111 operations.
- 48 readable in Inspect, 46 more in Edit project, 17 more in Full control.
- 31 land on Stacki's own undo stack.
- 53 capabilities deliberately kept out.
